map.Lessons 4-3, 4-4 & 4-5 — estimate percen: Lessons 4-3, 4-4 & 4-5: estimate percents, find them for real, then work them backward. Four reader gates stand between the night market and its goal.
map.Previously: the hundred-bulb lantern boa: Last time: the lantern board with a hundred bulbs showed the whole market that percent means per hundred. Distortion level: still flickering near Bram's stall.
map.Previously, in Episode 1: Hana's lantern: Last time, in Episode 1: Hana's lantern board turned the pier goal into one hundred glowing bulbs. Even Bram had to say what "per hundred" means. Tonight the festival is in full swing.
map.Halfway night! I'm running the fund trac: It's halfway night! I run the fund tracker. Every pledge gets chalked, checked, and added to the thermometer.
map.No time to double-check anything, kids!: No time to check twice, kids! Sales this hot check themselves!
map.For the record: nothing at that stall ha: Just so you know: nothing at that stall has ever been checked twice. Tonight we keep OUR numbers honest. Fast ones first.
map.The games alley. Tokens everywhere, and: The games alley. Tokens are everywhere. The line will not wait for long division.
map.Booth rules: 24% of these 81 ring-toss t: Booth rules: 24% of these 81 ring-toss tokens win prize stamps. The line wants a number NOW, not a worksheet.
map.So estimate it. 24% is one step from a b: So estimate it. 24% is close to a benchmark, and benchmarks are fast.
map.Estimation protocol: trade ugly numbers: Estimation rule: swap ugly numbers for friendly ones. Change the percent to a benchmark: 10%, 25%, or 50%. Then change the number to one that works well with it.
map.To estimate a percent of a number, round: To estimate a percent of a number, round both. Make the percent a friendly benchmark. Make the number one that divides evenly. Close and fast beats exact and late.
map.Speed round, reader — two estimates, zer: Speed round, reader! Two estimates, no calculators. The line is watching.
map.No calculators in the games alley. Snap: No calculators in the games alley. Change each percent to a friendly benchmark. Change each number to a friendly one. Then pick the best estimate.
map.Conceptual: estimating means trading for: Conceptual: estimating means using friendly numbers. 24% is right next to 25%, one quarter. 52% is right next to 50%, one half.
map.Procedural: a quarter of a number is the: Procedural: a quarter of a number is the number ÷ 4. 81 is close to 80. Half of a number is the number ÷ 2. 198 is close to 200.
map.Estimates got us through the rush. The l: Estimates got us through the rush. The ledger wants the REAL numbers. The fund can't save an "about."
map.Percent OF a number means multiply — aft: Percent OF a number means multiply. First, the percent must change into a decimal.
map.And once a percent becomes an amount, yo: Once a percent turns into an amount, you can compare it to real dollars.
map.To find a percent of a number, rewrite t: To find a percent of a number, write the percent as a decimal (30% = 0.30). Then multiply. The ÷100 is hiding in the % sign.
map.Reader — chalk the real amounts. The led: Reader, chalk the real amounts. The ledger does not take "about."
map.The ledger wants exact. The Garcia pledg: The ledger wants exact numbers. The Garcia pledge: 30% of $140 is paid tonight. The gift bundles: 15% of 60 lanterns are saved. Find both for real.
map.Conceptual: 'percent OF a number' means: Conceptual: 'percent OF a number' means multiply. First, the percent turns into a decimal. The ÷100 is hiding in the % sign.
map.Procedural: 30% = 0.30, so multiply 0.30: Procedural: 30% = 0.30, so multiply 0.30 × 140. Or find 10% of 140 and triple it. 15% = 0.15, so multiply 0.15 × 60. Or take 10% of 60 plus half of that again.
map.Closing-rush inventory. Two stalls, two: Closing-rush inventory. Two stalls, two counters. Nobody wrote down the starting totals.
map.This time we KNOW the part. The mystery: This time we KNOW the part. We need the whole. How big is the roll? How big is the batch?
map.Reverse protocol: whole = part ÷ percent: Reverse rule: whole = part ÷ percent-as-a-decimal. Dividing by a number less than one makes the part GROW back to its hundred. The whole is always bigger than its part.
map.The whole is the original 100%. Know a p: The whole is the original 100%. Know a part and its percent? Divide: whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal). Then check by multiplying.
map.Run it backwards, reader — rebuild both: Work backward, reader. Find both wholes before the restock cart leaves.
map.Closing-rush inventory. The booth sold 2: Closing-rush inventory. The booth sold 24 tickets. That is 40% of the roll. The stand sold 18 skewers. That is exactly 25% of tonight's batch. Find each WHOLE.
Conceptual: this time you KNOW the part. The whole is the original 100%. So the whole must be BIGGER than the part.
map.Procedural: whole = part ÷ (percent as a: Procedural: whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal). Tickets: 24 ÷ 0.40. Skewers: 18 ÷ 0.25. Then check by multiplying.
map.Late evening. The thermometer ticks past: Late evening. The thermometer passes its sixtieth bulb. Then Bram finds a megaphone.
map.Attention, market! Sixty percent done me: Listen, market! Sixty percent done means only SIXTY DOLLARS to go! Almost finished! Go home happy!
map.That's not how percents work — and if th: That is not how percents work. If the crowd believes him, the pledges will stop COLD.
map.Distortion spike. A percent is not an am: Distortion spike. A percent is not an amount. 60% only turns into dollars when it meets its whole. The crowd is about to leave. Work fast.
map.Three locks before the crowd drifts: the: Three locks before the crowd leaves: the FULL goal, what is still missing, and what went wrong in Bram's announcement.
The sign is honest. The megaphone is not. Reader, take on the boss.
map.Boss Gate: the thermometer gives you a p: Boss Gate: the thermometer gives you a part ($540) and its percent (60%). Work backward to the whole. Then work forward to what is left.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The thermometer: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The thermometer shows the part. You must find the whole.
map.The pier-fund thermometer reads $540 rai: The pier-fund thermometer reads $540 raised — 60% of the goal. Bram's megaphone says "60% done means only 60 dollars to go!" The crowd is leaving. Three locks:
map.Bram claims \"60% done means only 60 dol: Bram says "60% done means only 60 dollars to go!" What is his mistake?
map.Conceptual: $540 is the PART and 60% is: Conceptual: $540 is the PART and 60% is its percent. The goal is the WHOLE. Work backward to find it. Then see what is left to raise.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: goal = 540 ÷ 0.60. L: Procedural: Lock 1: goal = 540 ÷ 0.60. Lock 2: still needed = goal − 540. That is the 40% still left.
map.Nine hundred. Chalked, checked, and TRUE: Nine hundred. Chalked, checked, and TRUE. The crowd is back, and Bram holds the megaphone upside down in shame.
map.Fine. FINE. Three hundred sixty to go. I: Fine. FINE. Three hundred sixty to go. Next time I will… check the megaphone twice.
map.Estimate it.Snap the percent to a benchm: Estimate it.Change the percent to a benchmark (10%, 25%, 50%). Change the number to a friendly one. Close and fast beats exact and late.
map.Compute it.Percent OF a number = decimal: Compute it.Percent OF a number = decimal × number. The ÷100 is hiding in the % sign. 30% is 0.30, never just 30.
map.Reverse it.Know a part and its percent?: Reverse it.Know a part and its percent? whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal). The whole is always bigger than its part.
map.The megaphone trap.A percent is not an a: The megaphone trap.A percent is not an amount. "60%" only turns into dollars when it meets its whole. The whole was $900, not $600.
map.\"A percent without its whole is a rumor: "A percent without its whole is just a rumor. Find the whole, and the rumor becomes math." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 4 · Episode 2: Find the W: finished Unit 4 · Episode 2: Find the Whole and showed mastery of estimating percents, finding the percent of a number, and finding the whole from a part and its percent.
map.Different booth: about how much is 26% o: A new booth: about how much is 26% of 121 tokens?
map.One quarter of 120 = 30. So 26% of 121 i: One quarter of 120 = 30. So 26% of 121 is about 30. Fast and close enough for a festival line.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Different tag: 20% of a $35 crate goes t: A new tag: 20% of a $35 crate goes to the fund.
map.0.20 × 35 = 7 — so $7 to the fund. Decim: 0.20 × 35 = 7, so $7 goes to the fund. Decimal first, multiply second, every time.
map.Different stand: 21 cocoa cups is 30% of: A new stand: 21 cocoa cups is 30% of the night's supply.
21 ÷ 0.30 = 70 cups in the full supply. Check by multiplying: 0.30 × 70 = 21 ✓.
map.Different fund: $210 raised is 70% of a: A new fund: $210 raised is 70% of a smaller goal.
map.Still needed = 300 − 210 = $90 — which i: Still needed = 300 − 210 = $90. That is exactly the 30% left over. Part ÷ percent, then subtract.
map.Pick one estimate for EACH question, the: Pick one estimate for EACH question. Then check.
map.About 8 is the 10% benchmark of 81 — but: About 8 is the 10% benchmark of 81. But 24% is much closer to the QUARTER benchmark.
map.About 40 is HALF of 81 — the 50% benchma: About 40 is HALF of 81, the 50% benchmark. 24% is a much smaller slice.
map.About 60 is three quarters of 81 — way p: About 60 is three quarters of 81. That is more than 24%. First, round 24% to a benchmark.
About 10 of 198 is close to 5%. 52% is just over HALF. Think bigger.
map.About 150 is three quarters of 198. 52%: About 150 is three quarters of 198. 52% is only a little over half. Think smaller.
map.About 400 is DOUBLE 198 — a percent unde: About 400 is DOUBLE 198. A percent under 100 can never make the number bigger.
map.$42 tonight and 9 bundle lanterns — chal: $42 tonight and 9 bundle lanterns, written in ink. Exactly 30 per hundred, exactly 15 per hundred.
map.170 is 30 + 140 — that ADDS the percent: 170 is 30 + 140. That ADDS the percent as if it were dollars. 'Percent of' means multiply: 30% is 0.30 of the price.
map.4200 is 30 × 140 — but 30% isn't a plain: 4200 is 30 × 140. But 30% is not just 30. A percent hides a ÷100: use 0.30.
map.900 is 15 × 60 — that treats 15% like a: 900 is 15 × 60. That treats 15% as just 15. Move the decimal: 15% = 0.15 before you multiply.
map.So close — check the decimal point. 15%: So close! Check the decimal point. 15% = 0.15, and 0.15 × 60 must be far below 60.
map.The pledge first: turn 30% into a decima: Do the pledge first. Turn 30% into a decimal. Then multiply by 140. The answer is a part of 140, not more.
map.Now the lanterns: 15% = 0.15. Multiply b: Now the lanterns: 15% = 0.15. Multiply by 60. The saved pile is a small part of the crate.
map.A roll of 60 and a batch of 72 — both wh: A roll of 60 and a batch of 72. Both wholes are bigger than their parts. Both checked by multiplying. Inventory: honest.
map.24 × 0.40 = 9.6 — but the part should be: 24 × 0.40 = 9.6. But the part should be SMALLER than the whole. Did you shrink it? DIVIDE to grow 24 back to its 100%.
map.18 × 0.25 = 4.5 — but the part should be: 18 × 0.25 = 4.5. But the part should be SMALLER than the whole. Did you shrink it? DIVIDE 18 by the percent to find the batch.
map.Tickets: 24 is only 40 per hundred of th: Tickets: 24 is only 40 per hundred of the roll. Divide the part by 0.40. The roll must be bigger than 24.
map.Lock 1 holds. 540 × 0.6 shrinks the part: Lock 1 holds. 540 × 0.6 makes the part even smaller. But $540 already IS the 60%. Divide to find the whole.
map.Lock 2 holds. The thermometer is missing: Lock 2 holds. The thermometer is missing its last 40%. Take the full goal and subtract the $540 already in it.
map.Lock 3 holds. Bram didn't round — he swa: Lock 3 holds. Bram did not round. He mixed up UNITS. Look at what his '60' is counting.
map.Lock 3 holds. The sign's percent is hone: Lock 3 holds. The sign's percent is honest. Bram's mistake comes AFTER he reads it, when he says 'dollars' for 'percent.'
map.Lock 3 holds. If only $60 were missing,: Lock 3 holds. If only $60 were missing, $540 would be 90% of a $600 goal. But the sign says 60%. Pick what went wrong.
map.Lock 3 holds. Pick the answer that names: Lock 3 holds. Pick the answer that names Bram's mix-up.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Goal $900, $360 still to: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Goal $900, $360 still to go. Bram turned '60 PERCENT' into '60 DOLLARS.' A percent is not an amount until it meets its whole.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
